verses.text: By the will of God, our Lord Jesus Christ, Apostle Paul, and our brother Timothy,
To the saints in Colossae and to our brethren who are in Christ Jesus, grace and peace be unto you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
We give thanks to God the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, praying always for you.
Since the day we heard of your faith in Christ Jesus and of the love which ye have to all the saints, we do not cease to pray for you.
We pray that ye may be filled with the knowledge of His will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding, that ye may walk worthy of the Lord unto all pleasing.

This is so that you may be fruitful in every good work and increase in the knowledge of God, strengthened with all might, according to His glorious power, unto all patience and longsuffering with joyfulness.
For this cause we also, since the day we heard it, do not cease to pray for you, and to desire that ye might be filled with the knowledge of His will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding.
He also declared to us your love in the Spirit.

sections.title: A prayer concerning the teachers for the holy disciples.

verses.text: Therefore, from the moment we have heard your news, we strive to fulfill the will of the Lord God with perfect wisdom and with perfect spiritual counsel, and we have not ceased to pray and to intercede for you.
And as you go to the Lord, bearing fruit in every good work, seeking to know the Lord, may you be filled with all joy.
With perfect strength, with the might of His glory, with perfect patience, and with hope and joy, be steadfast.
Let us give thanks to the Lord, who has granted us a portion among the saints in light.
He has delivered us from darkness; and He has brought us to the kingdom of His beloved Son.
It is in our poverty that we have found Him, for our sins have been forgiven.
Behold, the Lord God, who is invisible, is above all creation.

By His word, the Lord has created all things; in heaven and on earth, that which is seen and that which is unseen, whether thrones or dominions, whether principalities or powers, all things were created through Him and for Him; all were created by His word.
He was before all things; and in Him all things consist.
He is the head of the church; for He is to all as a head, having risen from the dead before all the dead.
All things exist in Him, and He is complete.
He grants forgiveness to all through the blood that was shed upon the cross, and He established peace upon the earth and in the heavens.
And you were once estranged from God because of your thoughts and your wicked deeds, and you were enemies.
But now, you have been chosen to stand before Him, and you are holy; He will make you saints, and in your mortal flesh, He shall not hold you accountable for death.

sections.title: The Apostolic Ministry of Saint Paul

verses.text: Therefore, as I, Paul, a servant and messenger, have been appointed to you from heaven, I urge you to remain steadfast in the hope of the teaching of the Gospel, that you may be strengthened in faith.
Even now, in my affliction, I rejoice; for as my body is afflicted for the sake of the church, I bear the little suffering of Christ in my flesh.
Concerning you, I have been appointed as a messenger by the command of God.
The Lord has spoken, that the counsel which was hidden may be revealed, without the world being created, and without man being formed.
But today, the Lord has revealed this counsel of honor to the nations, that it may be made known to the saints whom He has chosen; for our glory is in you, and it is Christ who is with us.
And He, Jesus Christ, is the one whom we present as the perfect man, whom we teach to all men, to whom we call and to whom we offer our service, and His work we declare in all wisdom.
As He helps me with His power, I will rejoice in His aid; I will also give thanks.
For your sake and for those in Laodicea, I desire that you may know how great a struggle I have on behalf of all the saints who have not seen my face in the flesh.

That their hearts may be encouraged, being knit together in love, and attaining to all riches of the full assurance of understanding, to the knowledge of the mystery of God, both of the Father and of Christ, in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.
All the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden in Him.
This I say lest anyone should deceive you with persuasive words.
For though I am absent in the flesh, yet I am with you in spirit, rejoicing to see your good order and the steadfastness of your faith in Christ.
As you therefore have received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk in Him.
Rooted and built up in Him and established in the faith, as you have been taught, abounding in it with thanksgiving.
Beware lest anyone cheat you through philosophy and empty deceit, according to the tradition of men, according to the basic principles of the world, and not according to Christ.
For in Him dwells all the fullness of the Godhead bodily.
And you are complete in Him, who is the head of all principality and power.
He who has cast off the body of sin by the act of crucifixion, in Christ, has been crucified, and you have been crucified with Him.
In baptism, you have been buried with Him; and in His resurrection, you have been raised with Him through the help of God and in faith.
And you, being dead in your sins and in the uncircumcision of your flesh, were made alive together with Him; and all your sins He has forgiven you.
From our transgressions, He has raised us, having written the bond of our debt, and He has taken it out of the midst of us, nailing it to the cross.
By exposing the rulers and authorities, He made a public spectacle of them, triumphing over them in it.
Therefore, whether in eating or in drinking, or in special festivals, or in new moons, or on the Sabbath, take heed that none of these things may cause you to stumble.
All of this comes to pass for the sake of that warning. But the body is of Christ.
By prayer and by humbling oneself, you are commanded to offer supplication to the angels; and do not let your eyes be deceived by the empty counsel of the flesh.
All flesh is weak; in the flesh and in the spirit, it is weak; but in God, it is strengthened and is not weak in itself.
How then shall ye work, as those who dwell in this world, being dead with Christ?
How is it that ye do not renew this, do not consider this, and do not take heed to this?
For all this is as a command and teaching of man, unto destruction.
This is concerning the humility of the heart and the fear of God; it pertains to wisdom concerning the flesh and the vanity of the world; yet, it is above the flesh, for there is no glory therein.
If you have been raised with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God.
Set your mind on things that are above, not on things that are on the earth.
For you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God.
When Christ, who is your life, appears, then you also will appear with Him in glory.
Therefore, put to death your members which are on the earth: fornication, uncleanness, passion, evil desire, and covetousness, which is idolatry.
Because of these things, the wrath of God is coming upon the sons of disobedience.
In which you yourselves once walked when you lived in them.
But now you yourselves are to put off all these: anger, wrath, malice, blasphemy, and filthy language out of your mouth.
Do not lie to one another, since you have put off the old man with his deeds,
and have put on the new man who is renewed in knowledge according to the image of Him who created him.
In Him there is neither Jew nor Greek, neither circumcised nor uncircumcised, neither barbarian nor Scythian, neither bond nor free; but Christ is all, and in all.
Therefore, let the Lord, as He has chosen His saints and beloved ones, clothe you with mercy and kindness, humility and meekness, patience and forbearance.
Bear with one another; forgive one another, if any man have a quarrel against any; even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye.
And above all these things put on charity, which is the bond of perfectness.
And let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts, to the which also ye are called in one body; and be ye thankful.
Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.
And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by Him.

sections.title: Concerning the administration of the household.

verses.text: Wives, submit to your husbands as unto the Lord.
Husbands, love your wives; do not be harsh with them.
Children, obey your parents in all things; for this is well-pleasing to the Lord.
Fathers, do not provoke your children, lest they become discouraged.
Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh, not with eye-service, as men-pleasers, but in sincerity of heart, fearing God.
And whatever you do, do it heartily, as to the Lord and not to men.
Knowing that from the Lord you will receive the reward of the inheritance; for you serve the Lord Christ.
But he who does wrong will be repaid for what he has done, and there is no partiality.
ጌቶች ሆይ፥ ለአገልጋዮቻችሁ ትክክለኛውን አድርጉላቸው፤ እውነትንም ፍረዱ፤ በሰማይ ጌታ እንዳላችሁ ታውቃላችሁና።

sections.title: Concerning the spreading of the Gospel, let prayer be made as it is fitting.

verses.text: As you are gathered in thanksgiving, be devoted to prayer.
Concerning Him, that we may speak of the mystery of the Lord for which I have been imprisoned, may the Lord open to us the door of His word, and let us also pray for ourselves; for our sake.
That I may speak as it is fitting for me, grant me your prayers.
As you are changing the times, go forth in understanding from faith to those who are different.
That you may know how each one ought to respond, let your discourse always be seasoned with grace, as if it were seasoned with salt.

sections.title: The message of the teacher in the sacred psalm.

verses.text: Our beloved brother and faithful minister, who is also our fellow worker in the Lord, will make known to you my tidings.
Therefore, in order that you may know my tidings which I have sent to you concerning this work, it is to strengthen your hearts.
And if you are inquiring about our condition and our faithful brother Anasimos, they have reported to you our affairs and the state in which we stand.
The one who is with me, Aristarchus, a fellow prisoner, greets you, and Mark, the son of Barnabas, concerning whom you have received instructions; if he comes to you, welcome him.
Greetings to you from Jesus, who is called Justus; these are the only fellow workers for the kingdom of God who are of the circumcision. They have been a comfort to me.
Epaphras, who is one of you, greets you, a servant of Christ; he always strives for you in prayers, that you may stand perfect and complete in all the will of God.
For I bear him witness that he has a great zeal for you and those in Laodicea and those in Hierapolis.
Luke, the beloved physician, greets you, as does Demas.
Greet the brethren who are in Laodicea and Nymphas, and the church that is in his house.
Now when this epistle is read among you, see that it is read also in the church of the Laodiceans, and that you likewise read the epistle from Laodicea.
And say to Archippus, “Take heed to the ministry which you have received in the Lord, that you may fulfill it.”
This salutation by my own hand—Paul. Remember my chains. Grace be with you. Amen.
